normalized_issues.title: sequence_number removed from hashed columns without equivalent integrity guarantee

merged_from.title: Removing `sequence_number` from hashed columns breaks tamper-evidence for entry ordering metadata
`sequence_number` was removed from hash inputs without a replacement integrity rule

normalized_issues.core_problem: The v1.5.2 change removes `sequence_number` from `DhfHashColumns.HashedColumns` with the rationale that `previous_hash` enforces ordering. However, `previous_hash` proves link order between entries but does not protect the persisted `sequence_number` value on any individual row. A row can be renumbered, duplicated, or gaps introduced without invalidating `record_hash`. No compensating validator contract (e.g., `ValidateChainAsync` enforcing contiguous, unique sequence numbering) is defined in the spec.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Fran: '`previous_hash` proves link order, not the integrity of the current row's own `sequence_number`. A row can be renumbered, duplicated, or gaps introduced without changing `record_hash` unless chain validation separately enforces contiguous numbering. That validation is not stated here.' Codex: 'The spec no longer integrity-protects the persisted order field, and it does not define a validator contract that derives authoritative order solely from `previous_hash`.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either (a) restore `sequence_number` to `DhfHashColumns.HashedColumns`, or (b) explicitly define `ValidateChainAsync` as rejecting any non-contiguous or non-unique sequence numbering and add that requirement to ACC-02 and ACC-12. Option (b) requires the validator to walk the chain from genesis and derive expected sequence numbers from chain position, not from the stored field.

normalized_issues.title: PermanentlyFailed add-in state is unaddressed in SPEC-00 seams, glossary, and epoch semantics

merged_from.title: Incomplete propagation of SPEC-02 PermanentlyFailed state into SPEC-00 seams and glossary
Permanent-failure path discards the only evidence needed for the mandated post-timeout recovery record

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 v1.4.1 introduces a `PermanentlyFailed` terminal state where the add-in stops processing but does NOT exit the process and does NOT rotate AddinSessionId. SPEC-00 Seam B mandates that recovery events record whether post-timeout COM completion was detected, but in the permanent-failure scenario the late completion is explicitly discarded. Additionally, SPEC-00's session-closure model (Seam C, Glossary DHF Session, AddinSessionId epoch semantics) only accounts for `heartbeat_timeout`, `explicit_shutdown`, and `superseded_session` — none of which cleanly map to a live-but-permanently-failed add-in that never sends a teardown and never rotates its session ID. The close-and-new-session recovery model is broken for this path.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Grok: 'Creates unhandled edge case where subsequent reconnect reuses same AddinSessionId (no epoch rotation) or leaves dangling locked session; breaks the close-and-new-session model per SPEC-04 trigger design.' Fran: 'In the exact stuck-call scenario, the late completion is explicitly discarded after the add-in has entered PermanentlyFailed. The orchestration contract still requires the later recovery event to state whether post-timeout completion was detected... but no mechanism is defined to carry that evidence across restart/reconnect.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a `PermanentlyFailed` state to the SPEC-00 glossary and Seam B/C. Define: (1) what session closure reason is recorded when the orchestrator detects heartbeat timeout from a permanently-failed add-in; (2) whether AddinSessionId rotation is required before reconnect (it should be, since the add-in must be restarted); (3) a durable handoff mechanism for permanent-failure metadata (stuck CallId, tool name, eventual late-completion status) so SPEC-03 can append the mandated recovery event with evidence linkage on next session start. Add an ACC gate for this path.

normalized_issues.title: Permanent add-in failure reported to orchestrator using MalformedEnvelope error code

merged_from.title: Permanent add-in failure is misreported as `MalformedEnvelope`

normalized_issues.core_problem: SPEC-02 v1.4.1 step 7 specifies that when the add-in enters `PermanentlyFailed`, the `MessageDispatcher` rejects all incoming messages with `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = MalformedEnvelope, ...)`. `MalformedEnvelope` describes bad wire framing, not a terminal host failure. The orchestrator cannot distinguish protocol corruption from a permanently failed add-in, causing incorrect retry, quarantine, telemetry, and user-remediation behavior.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Codex: 'MalformedEnvelope describes bad wire framing, not an internal terminal host failure. The orchestrator cannot distinguish protocol corruption from a permanently failed add-in, so retry, quarantine, telemetry, and user-remediation behavior will be wrong.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Introduce a dedicated `AddinProtocolErrorMessage` error code (e.g., `PermanentlyFailed` or `AddinTerminalFailure`) for this condition. Define orchestrator handling: treat as terminal, do not retry, surface user-facing remediation ('Restart SolidWorks'), and record the session closure as `heartbeat_timeout` (or the new permanent-failure closure reason if R2-ISSUE-001 is addressed).

normalized_issues.title: Recovery event session target is undefined when prior session is already closed

merged_from.title: Recovery event append target is undefined after session-closing reconciliation

normalized_issues.core_problem: Seam C states that on next session start, if reconciliation detects model divergence, SPEC-03 records a reconciliation event via `DhfLedger.AppendRecoveryEventAsync`. However, the prior session has already been closed (via `heartbeat_timeout` or `superseded_session`). The spec does not define which `session_id` receives the recovery event: appending to the closed session conflicts with the closure invariant; appending to the new session breaks causal traceability unless a cross-session link is defined.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Codex: '`AppendRecoveryEventAsync` cannot be implemented consistently: appending to the closed session conflicts with the closure invariant, while appending to the new session breaks causal traceability unless a cross-session link is defined.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define per-trigger rules for recovery event session targeting. Recommended: recovery events from post-disconnect reconciliation are appended to the NEW session with explicit linkage fields (`source_session_id`, `source_entry_id`) pointing to the last entry of the prior session. Update `AppendRecoveryEventAsync` signature and `recovery_context` JSONB schema to carry these fields. Add an ACC gate.

normalized_issues.title: Reconnect semantics after heartbeat_timeout with same AddinSessionId are undefined

merged_from.title: Reconnect semantics after `heartbeat_timeout` with the same `AddinSessionId` are undefined

normalized_issues.core_problem: The glossary states AddinSessionId changes only on add-in reload, and DHF sessions are NOT closed on transient transport loss. But if transport loss exceeds the heartbeat timeout threshold, the session IS closed. If the add-in process is still running and reconnects with the same AddinSessionId after a heartbeat_timeout closure, the spec does not define whether SPEC-04 resumes, rejects, or opens a new session, nor how StateVersion and conflict checks behave.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Fran: 'The contract does not state what happens when transport loss exceeds the heartbeat timeout but the add-in process is still running and reconnects with the same AddinSessionId. It is unclear whether SPEC-04 must resume, reject, or open a new session with the same epoch, and how StateVersion and conflict checks behave in that case.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add an explicit rule to the AddinSessionId glossary entry and Seam C: when a session is closed due to `heartbeat_timeout` and the add-in reconnects with the same AddinSessionId, SPEC-04 opens a NEW DHF session (same AddinSessionId, new session row). StateVersion does NOT reset (no epoch rotation). SPEC-03 performs state reconciliation before the first new turn. Add an ACC gate for this reconnect path.

normalized_issues.title: PendingDecoration uses raw JsonElement with no canonical schema, validation owner, or module ownership

merged_from.title: Cross-module type ownership gap for PendingDecoration/PendingDecorations after co-transactional change
Decoration persistence seam uses raw `JsonElement` instead of a canonical cross-module contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: The co-transactional decoration fix (R1-ISSUE-001) introduces `PendingDecoration` with a `JsonElement Payload` field that crosses four module boundaries (SPEC-07 → SPEC-05 → SPEC-03 → SPEC-04) with no shared schema, required fields list, `schemaVersion` field, or validation owner defined at any seam. The prose names `VocabularyResolutionDecoration` as a specific type but the actual contract is untyped JSON. No module is designated as the canonical owner of this type in the Module Map.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Codex: 'The prose names a specific decoration type, but the actual seam contract is untyped JSON with no shared schema, required fields list, or validation owner defined at the boundary. SPEC-07, SPEC-05, SPEC-04, and SPEC-06 can drift independently; malformed or version-skewed decorations can be persisted without deterministic rejection.' Grok: 'No owning module declares the canonical PendingDecoration record or its JSON schema; SPEC-00 treats it as implicit contract across four modules without definition in Module Map or SPEC-01 shared types.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define a formal `VocabularyResolutionDecoration` JSON schema (including `schemaVersion` and required fields) owned by SPEC-07. Specify that SPEC-04's `AppendTurnAsync` validates the payload against the schema before persisting (or delegates validation to a shared validator). Add `PendingDecoration` to the Module Map ownership column for SPEC-04 (as the persistence contract) and reference SPEC-07 as the schema owner. Consider whether `PendingDecoration` should be a typed record in a shared assembly rather than raw `JsonElement`.

normalized_issues.title: Cross-workstation conflict enforcement relies on an untrusted client-supplied workstation_id field

merged_from.title: Cross-workstation conflict enforcement relies on an explicitly untrusted client field

normalized_issues.core_problem: The SPEC-04 v1.5.2 change adds a hard-error cross-workstation conflict check using `workstation_id != @WorkstationId`. The Deployment doc explicitly states `workstation_id` is a 'client-supplied string, not a trust boundary' accepted at face value. A client can spoof another workstation name to bypass the conflict check or cause false conflicts, making ACC-19 and the cross-workstation safety invariant non-authoritative.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Fran: 'The hard-error collision rule depends on `workstation_id`, but the same document says that value is accepted at face value and is not trustworthy. A client can spoof another workstation name to bypass the conflict check or cause false conflicts. This makes ACC-19 and the cross-workstation safety invariant non-authoritative.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: For v1: either (a) introduce a server-issued persistent workstation token (stored in Windows Credential Manager alongside API key) that the orchestrator issues and validates, making workstation identity server-trustworthy, or (b) downgrade the cross-workstation check to observability-only (log warning, do not throw) and remove the hard-error guarantee from ACC-19 and the contract. Document the chosen approach in the Deployment doc §6 and SPEC-04 SDR-04-008.

normalized_issues.title: Session closure reasons are ephemeral (7-day Railway log retention) with no durable export path

merged_from.title: Session closure reasons expire after 7 days because they are only logged, not durably stored

normalized_issues.core_problem: Closure reasons (`explicit_shutdown`, `heartbeat_timeout`, `superseded_session`) are recorded only in Serilog structured logs with Railway's default 7-day retention. Operators investigating older sessions cannot determine why a session ended. The spec acknowledges this is observability-grade, but provides no durable export path or minimum retention requirement.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Codex: 'SPEC-00: Closure reasons are recorded in the orchestrator's structured logs, NOT in the DHF schema. DEPLOYMENT §7: Retention: Railway default (7 days). The only authoritative source for closure attribution is an ephemeral log sink with short retention.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either (a) require a durable log export sink (e.g., export to S3 or a long-retention observability store) with a defined minimum retention period, or (b) persist a non-hash-chain closure-reason record in a separate `dhf.session_events` table (outside the hash chain, clearly marked as observability-grade). Document the chosen approach in Deployment §7 and SPEC-00 §6 DHF Session glossary entry.

normalized_issues.title: Auth-mode detection via /health WWW-Authenticate header has no defined response contract

merged_from.title: Auth-mode detection relies on an unspecified `/health` negotiation contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: The Deployment doc §2 Migration Mechanism states the add-in detects auth mode by inspecting the `WWW-Authenticate` header on an HTTPS probe to `/health`. No response contract is defined: HTTP method, status codes, header values for each mode, auth requirements for the probe itself, and proxy/header-stripping behavior are all unspecified.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Codex: 'No response contract is defined for `/health`: method, status codes, header values, auth requirements, and proxy/header-stripping behavior are all unspecified. The add-in cannot implement or test v1/v2 auth-mode negotiation deterministically.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either (a) define the exact `/health` endpoint contract (unauthenticated GET, 200 OK, `WWW-Authenticate: ApiKey` for v1 / `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm=...` for v2, with example responses and fallback behavior), or (b) replace runtime probing with an explicit configured auth mode (env var or build-time constant) and remove the probing mechanism entirely. Option (b) is simpler for a hackathon scope.

normalized_issues.title: Global flat ACC numbering scheme generates recurring renumbering churn and collision risk

merged_from.title: Brittle global ACC numbering scheme still generating renumbering churn and master-table collisions

normalized_issues.core_problem: The single flat master ACC table without module prefixes has already required renumbering twice (ACC-20 from SPEC-06's original ACC-08; ACC-28/29/30 from SPEC-07's original ACC-25/26/27). Each renumbering requires coordinated changes across SPEC-00 and the owning module spec, creating governance overhead and collision risk as more modules are integrated.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Grok: 'ACC-28 through ACC-30 were renumbered from SPEC-07's original ACC-25/26/27 in v1.2.0 to resolve the global namespace collision with SPEC-00/SPEC-04's ACC-25/26/27 (R1-ISSUE-004). Direct evidence of scope drift and governance failure in the integration contract role of SPEC-00.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Replace global flat numbering with module-namespaced IDs (e.g., `VOCAB-01`, `DHF-01`, `PROTO-01`) in per-module specs. The SPEC-00 master table references these namespaced IDs directly. This eliminates collision risk and removes the need for renumbering when new modules are added. Alternatively, reserve explicit numeric ranges per module (e.g., SPEC-07 owns ACC-21–40) and document the reservation in SPEC-00 §3.

normalized_issues.title: SDR-TL-009 absolute BSMS prohibition may be infeasible for incomplete CAD corpus coverage

merged_from.title: SDR-TL-009's absolute BSMS-only lock ignores CAD domain incompleteness and locks out viable alternatives

normalized_issues.core_problem: SDR-TL-009 prohibits all vector retrieval absolutely and permanently ('It will never be FAISS'). Parametric CAD, user-defined features, custom materials, and standards variants make exhaustive structured corpus coverage difficult. Frequent bouncer rejections due to corpus gaps become a UX failure mode. The four rationales for BSMS superiority are stated without analysis of the hybrid case.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Grok: 'Parametric CAD + user-defined features, custom materials, and standards variants make exhaustive structured corpus impossible; frequent bouncer rejections or missing citations become core UX failure mode unaddressed by the four rationales. What-if-opposite assumption (hybrid vector + structured fallback is superior for geometric/semantic similarity in CAD) is dismissed without analysis.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: This is a strategic architectural decision within the authors' purview. The finding is noted as a feasibility concern but is weak signal for a hackathon-scope spec — the 9-tool demo corpus is well-defined. If the authors wish to address it, add a corpus-completeness risk section to SPEC-07 acknowledging the gap and defining the bouncer rejection UX for out-of-corpus queries.

dropped_findings.title: SDR-TL-009's absolute BSMS-only lock ignores CAD domain incompleteness and locks out viable alternatives
dropped_findings.reason: Retained as R1-ISSUE-013 (recurring) but downgraded to low/weak_signal — this is a strategic architectural choice within the authors' purview, not a spec defect. The hackathon corpus is well-scoped.
